summary: Full end-to-end verification of the Stripe test-mode paywall. Backend 10/10 pytest cases passing in /app/backend/tests/test_paywall.py: GET /api/payments/credits returns correct shape {can_run, free_used, paid_credits, total_runs, price} — with 13+ existing runs, free_used=true, can_run=false, paid_credits=0. All three run endpoints (POST /api/engine/run, /api/engine/run-panel, /api/prototype/run) correctly return HTTP 402 with 'Payment required' message when no credits available. POST /api/payments/checkout creates a real Stripe test session — checkout_url starts with https://checkout.stripe.com and session_id is returned; a payment_transactions record is inserted. GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} returns {session_id, status, payment_status} for the created session and 404 for invalid ids. Regression endpoints /api/health and /api/persona-panels still return 200. Frontend verified via Playwright at REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: /persona-panels renders PaywallGate banner ('Free run used — Purchase a run credit ($1.00) to continue testing') positioned between persona cards and run bar, data-testid=paywall-gate and data-testid=paywall-purchase-btn present, 'Run this panel' button is disabled. /prototype renders paywall-gate above the run config section. /payment/success mounts and shows Spinner + 'Confirming payment...' initially (transitions to error state on invalid session). /payment/cancel shows 'Payment cancelled' with 'Back to app' button (data-testid=payment-cancel-back). All other pages (/, /new-run, /reports, /cross-stage-diff, /generate-panel) load with HTTP 200 and no console/page errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Payment.jsx uses raw axios + local `${process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL}/api` instead of shared /lib/api.js — same DRY violation flagged in prior iterations.

usePaywall hook fetches /api/payments/credits on mount but does not refresh after a payment success — user has to reload the page after paying. Consider calling refresh() on window focus or when returning from /payment/success.

consume_credit in paywall.py has a small race: total_runs is counted first and then a paid credit update is attempted; two concurrent first-time users could both see total_runs==0 and get 'free run' — very unlikely in single-user test tool but worth noting.
Stripe amount is hard-coded server-side (good), but the client Payment.jsx uses a hard-coded price string ($1.00) in usePaywall banner text; if RUN_PRICE changes in paywall.py the UI would drift.
PaymentSuccess polls every 2s up to 15 attempts (30s max); no visual indication of remaining time — minor UX polish.
server.py: `from emergentintegrations.payments.stripe.checkout import CheckoutSessionRequest` sits between endpoints (line 248) — move all imports to top of file.
server.py remains 1291 lines; router split still recommended (payments/paywall could easily be split into a submodule).
seed_data_creation: One pending payment_transactions record inserted during checkout test (session_id from Stripe test mode, payment_status=pending, credit_used=false). Not marked paid — safe to remain or be cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Paywall feature verified end-to-end. All 3 run endpoints properly gate with 402 when can_run=false. Checkout session creation works with sk_test_emergent. If the tester wants to fully verify the paid flow, they must complete a Stripe checkout (test card 4242 4242 4242 4242) — I did NOT complete a payment per instruction. The pending payment_transactions record from my checkout test remains in Mongo; consuming logic filters on payment_status='paid' so it won't affect can_run. To reset the paywall state (make can_run=true again), either (a) complete a Stripe test checkout or (b) manually insert a payment_transactions doc with payment_status='paid' and credit_used=false. Backend test file at /app/backend/tests/test_paywall.py is a stable regression suite for this feature.
